column1: # Basidiomycete yeast biofilm / adhesion candidate seeds (DRAFT - literature survey 2026-09-27)
# PROVENANCE. Hand-curated from PubMed (searched 2026-09-27), UniProtKB REST
# (rest.uniprot.org), InterPro/Pfam, and the FungiDB community gene-name table for
# which is the source used to map published gene names (CFL1, CPL1, DHA1, ZNF2, MP88,
# PBX1/2, BLP1, CIG1, CPS1) to CNAG_ locus tags. CNAG -> UniProt accessions were then
# resolved by querying rest.uniprot.org with the locus tag restricted to taxonomy_id:235443.
# DHA2 (CNAG_06082) and CFL105 (CNAG_03454) are NOT in the FungiDB name table; their loci
# come from PMID 28039134 (Gyawali et al. 2017) and were confirmed to be the remaining two
# Pfam PF21671 members of the H99 proteome.
# Style follows data/curated/adhesins/literature_seeds.tsv. Nothing here has been reviewed
# by a human expert. NO accession in this file was guessed: uniprot_query is blank wherever
# the literature does not let an accession be resolved, and evidence_summary says so.
#   gene                 published gene/protein name, or "(none identified)" for an
#                        organism-level phenotype with no gene attached
#   uniprot_query        UniProtKB query string (accession:X, or a Pfam+taxon family query
#                        for candidate pools). BLANK = unresolved, see evidence_summary.
#   class                adhesin                    experimentally supported adhesion function
#                        adhesin_candidate          named gene, adhesion inferred, not shown
#                        adhesin_candidate_family   unnamed family pool for a clade
#                        surface_candidate          surface glycoprotein, no adhesion assay
#                        surface_effector           surface/secreted, function is NOT adhesion
#                        hard_negative_candidate    surface look-alike, evidence argues against adhesion
#                        not_a_protein              flagged so it is never harvested as a positive
#                        phenotype_only             adhesion/biofilm phenotype, no gene known
#   evidence_level       E1 direct experimental adhesion/binding (deletion or binding assay)
#                        E2 family membership, or weaker phenotype (biofilm-only, overexpression,
#                        n/a for rows where the adhesin scale does not apply
#   direction            promotes | restrains | unknown | n/a   (GO involved_in does NOT encode
# TWO THINGS TO READ BEFORE USING THIS FILE
#   1. The Cryptococcus capsule polysaccharide GXM is NOT a protein. Cryptococcal biofilm
#      depends on it (PMID 16177306, 17513597), so "Cryptococcus biofilm factor" in the
#      literature very often means a polysaccharide or a polysaccharide-biosynthesis enzyme,
#      not an adhesin. Rows flagged not_a_protein / hard_negative_candidate mark these.
#   2. Family membership in the Cfl1/CPL1 (SIGC, Pfam PF21671) family does NOT imply adhesion:
#      Cfl1 is an adhesin (PMID 22737071) while its paralog Cpl1 is a secreted immune effector
#      acting through TLR4 with no reported adhesion role (PMID 35896747).

column4: Cfl1/CPL1-like, C-terminal SIGC cysteine-rich domain (Pfam PF21671)
column10: First adhesin described in the Basidiomycota; Znf2 downstream target; cfl1 perturbation alters morphogenesis, cell adhesion, biofilm formation and virulence; secreted, shed into the ECM and acts as a paracrine autoinducer; signal peptide and the C-terminal SIGC domain are both required for adherence and signalling. CNAG_00795 (FungiDB community name table, PMID 22737071) -> UniProt J9VHS9, 309 aa, SignalP 1-18, no GPI annotated.

Overexpression gave strong adherence to glass and visibly increased colony wrinkledness, the same readouts as CFL1oe; secretion confirmed. No deletion phenotype reported, so adhesion is not formally demonstrated. Locus CNAG_03454 from PMID 28039134 (not in the FungiDB name table); UniProt J9VVN7, 409 aa, SignalP 1-23.

Secreted, expressed in all cell types and enriched at basidia; induced by copper limitation and repressed by excess copper. Overexpression gave only modest adherence in C. neoformans. The Trichosporon asahii ortholog is strongly induced in biofilm (PMID 41627572), which is the main reason it is listed. Adhesion itself not demonstrated. CNAG_07422 -> UniProt J9VSS0, 327 aa.

Yeast-form-specific secreted member of the Cfl1 family; secretion confirmed, adherence effect on overexpression only modest. No adhesion or biofilm assay. Locus CNAG_06082 from PMID 28039134 (not in the FungiDB name table); UniProt J9VY16, 317 aa.

column4: Cfl1/CPL1-like (Pfam PF21671, the family's type protein)
column10: IMPORTANT NEGATIVE CONTROL. Secreted effector that drives M2/alternative polarization of macrophages via host TLR4 and is essential for virulence; no adhesion or biofilm phenotype reported. Same domain family as the adhesin Cfl1, so PF21671 membership alone must not be treated as adhesin evidence. CNAG_02797 -> UniProt J9VQE5 (reviewed), 199 aa.

Master regulator of the yeast-to-hypha transition; necessary and sufficient for filamentation. Its effect on morphotype and pathogenicity is mediated at least partly through cell adhesion properties, and Cfl1 is its prominent downstream adhesion target. Note the sign flip: ZNF2 overexpression promotes adhesion/filamentation but ABOLISHES virulence. CNAG_03366 (FungiDB community name table) -> UniProt J9VT45, 738 aa.

Targeted deletion links this calcineurin-responsive/PKC1-dependent TF to cell integrity, survival under limited aeration, fluconazole susceptibility AND biofilm formation. The abstract does not state whether the mutant makes more or less biofilm, so direction is left unknown rather than assumed. CNAG_00156 -> UniProt J9VE33 (reviewed).

Immunoreactive T-cell-stimulating mannoprotein with a C-terminal Ser/Thr-rich (O-glycosylated) region and a predicted GPI site; the paper notes at least 11 further H99 genes share this architecture, i.e. this is the closest cryptococcal analogue of the ascomycete GPI-CWP pool. In a GPI-anchored-protein mutant screen the CNAG_00776 mutant showed impaired growth under plasma-membrane stress and significantly decreased phagocytosis. No adhesion or binding assay. CNAG_00776 -> UniProt J9VF18, 378 aa.

CNAG_00137, one of two hits from a systematic screen of 47 predicted GPI-anchored proteins; mutant impaired for cell-wall stress and elevated temperature and significantly reduced in phagocytosis. No published gene name, so the gene column is intentionally blank. UniProt J9VI39, 323 aa, SignalP 1-26.

Proposed HARD NEGATIVE. GPI-anchored, signal-peptide-bearing, glycosylated cell-wall/secreted protein with a defined catalytic activity (chitin deacetylase) and no adhesion function. Architecturally the kind of protein the current stage-1 model calls positive. CNAG_01230 -> UniProt J9VND2 (reviewed), 455 aa.

Proposed HARD NEGATIVE and an explicit confounder: pbx1 deletion gives dry colonies and CLUMPY CELLS, i.e. an aggregation phenotype, but the demonstrated molecular role is fidelity of GXM capsule polysaccharide synthesis, not adhesion. A cell-aggregation phenotype in Cryptococcus is not evidence of an adhesin. CNAG_01172 -> UniProt J9VL58, 606 aa, SignalP 1-18.

As PBX1: deletion gives dry colony morphology, clumpy cells, decreased capsule integrity and aberrant GXM linkages; attenuated virulence. Role is capsule polysaccharide synthesis, not adhesion. CNAG_05562 -> UniProt J9W1W2, 704 aa.

Gat201-bound gene accounting for much of the capsule-INDEPENDENT antiphagocytic activity; a small secreted surface effector whose function is phagocytosis inhibition, not adhesion. Useful as a surface-but-not-adhesin label. CNAG_06346 -> UniProt J9W0U6 (reviewed), 138 aa.

Extracellular/GPI-anchored mannoprotein whose transcript rises under iron limitation; cig1 disruption impairs low-iron growth and alters the capsule response. No adhesion assay; listed as a surface glycoprotein of known identity, likely a stage-1 positive and stage-2 negative. CNAG_01653 -> UniProt J9VUB8.

The adhesion phenotype here belongs to a POLYSACCHARIDE, not a protein: cps1 loss and hyaluronidase treatment both reduce binding to human brain microvascular endothelial cells, and binding is proportional to hyaluronic acid content; the host receptor is CD44. Cps1 is a membrane-bound synthase, NOT a surface adhesin. Caveat: the Neurospora ortholog CPS-1 makes a cell-wall polysaccharide that is NOT hyaluronic acid (PMID 24953997), so the HA assignment is not settled. CNAG_04320 -> UniProt J9VUH0.

FLAG ROW, DELIBERATELY HAS NO ACCESSION. Cryptococcal biofilm formation requires the polysaccharide capsule and correlates with the ability of capsular polysaccharide to bind the solid support; anti-GXM antibody blocks biofilm when in solution but PROMOTES it when surface-coated (immobilization); EDTA blocks biofilm by reducing GXM shedding and vesicle secretion. The dominant cryptococcal biofilm "adhesive" is therefore a sugar. Any protein-level biofilm label for Cryptococcus must be read against this background.

column4: Cfl1/CPL1-like (Pfam PF21671; InterPro IPR048661; PANTHER PTHR35192 PriA/Cpl1_fungi)
column10: qRT-PCR across four strains: dramatic and uniform upregulation in biofilm relative to planktonic growth. In silico docking predicted binding to albumin, collagen IV, fibronectin, hemoglobin and laminin. uniprot_query BLANK: the paper names the genes only by homology to C. neoformans and gives no locus tag or accession, and the strains used (CBS2479, CBS7631, L2585, L773) are not the sequenced UniProt strain. The T. asahii var. asahii CBS 8904 proteome contains 8 PF21671 members (A1Q2_07842, A1Q2_03191, A1Q2_03930, A1Q2_00039, A1Q2_05189, A1Q2_00505, A1Q2_00709, A1Q2_01196) but the 1:1 ortholog assignment is unresolved and is NOT guessed here.
Strongly induced under biofilm conditions in all four strains tested. Same accession caveat as T. asahii CFL1: no locus tag published.
Expression varied by strain and morphotype; no clear biofilm direction reported. No accession published.

Preferentially expressed in the yeast form even during biofilm formation, i.e. NOT biofilm-induced; consistent with the C. neoformans Cpl1 being an immune effector rather than an adhesin. No accession published.

column4: repellent (Rep1 repeat, Pfam PF29797); 11 KEX2-cleaved secreted peptides
column10: rep1 deletion abolishes attachment of hyphae to hydrophobic Teflon, makes colonies completely wettable and abolishes aerial hyphae; repellents, not hydrophobins, mediate attachment in U. maydis. ALREADY PRESENT in data/curated/adhesins/literature_seeds.tsv; repeated here so the basidiomycete picture is complete in one place. PF29797 is restricted to Ustilaginomycotina.

Proposed HARD NEGATIVE with DIRECT negative evidence: deleting hum2, or hum2 and hum3 together, left surface hydrophobicity essentially unaffected and did not affect attachment to hydrophobic Teflon; the authors conclude hydrophobins have been functionally replaced by repellents in this species. A hydrophobin is therefore not automatically an adhesin. UniProt A0A0D1BZL3 (gene hum2, UMAG_11562), 118 aa.

column4: class I hydrophobin preceded by 17 KEX2-separated repeats
column10: hum3 single deletion has no pathogenicity phenotype, but the hum3 rsp1 double mutant stops early after plant penetration and is completely non-pathogenic; yeast-like growth, mating, aerial hyphae formation and surface hydrophobicity were all UNAFFECTED, so the phenotype is host penetration rather than demonstrated adhesion. Listed E2 with that caveat. NOTE: UniProt gives the gene name as "him3" (UMAG_04433) with protein name "Class I hydrophobin hum3" - verify this name mismatch in review.

column4: Rep1-like repetitive secreted protein, 11 KEX2-cleaved peptides
column10: Secreted repetitive protein sharing the Rep1 repeat architecture; essential together with hum3 for pathogenic development immediately after penetration. Adhesion not directly assayed. UniProt A0A0D1DPX0 (UMAG_06112), 260 aa.

CANDIDATE POOL, NO EXPERIMENTAL EVIDENCE IN THIS GENUS. UniProt holds 92 PF21671 proteins across the genus Rhodotorula (14+ in R. toruloides alone), making it one of the largest expansions of this basidiomycete-specific secreted family outside Kwoniella and Puccinia. Nothing in PubMed connects any Rhodotorula protein to adhesion: the queries "Rhodotorula adhesin gene" and "Rhodotorula mucilaginosa catheter adhesion" both return zero hits (2026-09-27). Genus-level query given instead of an accession, on purpose.

ORGANISM-LEVEL PHENOTYPE ONLY, NO GENE. R. mucilaginosa showed the highest cell-surface hydrophobicity and the best adhesion properties among yeasts co-isolated from spoiled soft drinks (PMID 29058139); insect dispersal of Rhodotorula is mediated partly by adhesion of the yeast to insect cuticle via hydrophobic interactions (PMID 42296353); R. mucilaginosa biofilms on catheter-relevant surfaces are eradicable by gemini surfactants (PMID 23827647, 25843277) and the genus is listed among device-associated biofilm formers (PMID 24252828). No protein has ever been assigned to any of this.

NO CANDIDATE PROTEIN EXISTS. Malassezia furfur clinical isolates are hydrophobic, adherent and biofilm-forming, with hydrophobicity/adherence/biofilm correlated in ~60% of strains (PMID 28340187), and M. pachydermatis forms biofilm on polystyrene and polyurethane catheters (PMID 17510859, 22682201). Adhesion to keratinocytes is partly mediated by HOST cell-surface glycosaminoglycans, not by an identified fungal protein (PMID 34052141). Critically, the M. sympodialis/M. globosa genome paper reports that Malassezia species "do not appear to have many cell wall-localized GPI proteins and lack other cell wall proteins previously identified in other fungi" (PMID 23341551); consistent with that, UniProt returns ZERO PF21671 proteins in the genus Malassezia. This is a genuine biological absence, not a curation gap.
